messages.content:
Simulate a fictional lost-sales inventory system exactly. There is no stochastic prediction and no missing information beyond the explicit reporting cutoff.
Receipts add quantity to stock. Demands consume min(stock, quantity); any unmet quantity is lost (never backlogged). A stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, not merely ending with zero stock.
For raw report histories: first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id. Revisions REPLACE earlier reports, not add to them. Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order.
The canonical arm supplies the already selected eligible events in event-time order. The snapshot arm supplies the exactly replayed historical state. These are explicitly identified, executable preprocessing interventions.
After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future.
Return five integers through submit_answer: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after the scenario; future_lost for the scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if no future demand is unmet. Do not count historical stockouts in that last field.

Now we have a representation:

Eligible events: a set of events with fields event_id, revision (they are all revision 1? Yes) event_time, received_time, kind, quantity. We need to handle revisions: we first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff (100). Then for each event_id (each unique event), if there are multiple revisions (multiple reports), we choose the highest visible revision (max revision number) for each event_id. In this particular data set, each event_id appears only once with revision=1, so it's straightforward.

Then we keep chosen events where event_time <= target_time (100). We apply those events in order sorted by (event_time, event_id). Apply to initial_stock to compute stock_at_target (stock after all events up to target_time). Also compute total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions (i.e., total unmet demand from historical events up to target_time). Also need to note any stockout occurrences may be used for future stockout detection but we only want first_future_stockout_time later.

Then we ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. So if received_time > knowledge_cutoff, we ignore that event even if its event_time <= target_time. Here all eligible events have received_time at most 85, so all visible.

No revisions more than 1.

Now after the historical reconstruction, we apply every event in the given future_schedule, in order sorted by (event_time, event_id), starting from the reconstructed stock after target_time. This is the scenario future events. We need to compute:
- stock_at_horizon: after applying all future events up to horizon_time (130). Actually horizon_time is given as 130. All future events in schedule have event times up to 128. So all will be applied. The stock after all future events at horizon_time.

- future_lost: total lost demand from the scenario ONLY (i.e., future events), presumably counting unmet demand across all future events regardless of lost that happened historically. But the spec says "future_lost for the scenario ONLY". So we need to sum unmet demand for these future events. Not include any previously lost units from past events.

- first_future_stockout_time: earliest future scenario event time where unmet demand >0 (i.e., a stockout). If no unmet demand in any future event, output -1.
